question: to the Commission Aurore Lalucq (S&D) Subject:

In its 2024 special report, the European Court of Auditors (ECA) concluded that the Commission had not conducted a sufficiently rigorous evaluation of the application of the Interchange Fee Regulation (IFR)1, adopted in 2015. The court notably found that evaluation work is significantly overdue, and that several Member States are not correctly implementing the interchange fee caps, to the detriment of European merchants. 1.
What concrete measures does the Commission intend to take in response to the ECA’s findings regarding the shortcomings in the implementation of the IFR, and according to what timeline?

Does the Commission plan to carry out a new, thorough and independent evaluation of the application of the IFR across all Member States, in order to ensure effective compliance with interchange fee caps – and if so, within what timeframe?
Regulation (EU) 2015/751 of 29 April 2015 on interchange fees for card-based payment transactions (ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2015/751/oj). 1
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (7.8.2026) The 2020 Report1 to the European Parliament and the Council on the impact of the Interchange Fee Regulation (IFR) 2015/751 (‘the Regulation’), the underlying study2 to the 2020 Report and the 2024 study – the latter focusing in particular on areas for further monitoring and reinforced data gathering identified in the 2020 Report3, all concluded that the Regulation is working well, including the caps on interchange fees across the EU. As highlighted in the Commission’s replies to the European Court of Auditors’ (ECA) Report4, the 2024 study suggested that merchant service charges may be on the rise for debit cards transactions while charges for credit card transactions may be decreasing, based on a limited merchant survey (2024 study page 95). In addition, it is worth noting that the current caps on interchange fees for consumer debit and credit cards under the Regulation are low compared to other jurisdictions5. The Commission reviewed the application of the Regulation in line with its review clause under the 2020 Report, concluding in particular that it was too early ‘to decide on the necessity of a legislative proposal to review the IFR’. While at this stage another study is not envisaged, the Commission is in regular contact with the national competent authorities to foster consistent implementation, closely monitors developments in retail payment markets and actively investigates when relevant.
